fleet_kv_note: KV-DEPENDENT, WAS BROKEN, NOW SELF-HEALING (verified live this session, corrected mid-build): this job's Azure config resolves Key Vault access via an Azure Container Apps managed identity (or the vestigial legacy sab64/GCP path), and its AWS task definition carries the same AZURE_KEYVAULT_NAME (+ AZURE_UAMI_CLIENT_ID where Azure had one) forward for capture-fidelity with the existing 22's own precedent -- NEITHER is directly functional on ECS Fargate (no Azure managed identity exists there, no AZURE_SP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET is wired). Reading the 2026-08-16 03:57 Terraform capture alone, this looked like a hard blocker for 11 of the pre-existing 22 twins (brain-reindex, daily-digest, deep-finance, deep-legal-company, deep-legal-personal, fleet-backup, fleet-secret-custodian, librarian-commerce, librarian-finance, librarian-legal-company, librarian-legal-personal) plus up to 9 of the 10 new jobs. IT IS NOT A BLOCKER TODAY: skills/kb-memory/aws-secret.mjs (an automatic Key-Vault-then-SSM cross-cloud fallback inside the SAME kvSecret() every doc-indexer job script calls) merged to main in 6dee16d, the same commit as cutover-preflight, evidently a concurrent sibling wave working this same emergency. Independently verified live this session (not merely read): a real SigV4-signed SSM GetParameter succeeded for azure-foundry-key, azure-openai-key, and posthog-fleet-ingest-key using the aws-cto-* credential path, and the deployed otchealthTaskRole (used by every job task def, old and new) already carries ssm:GetParameter{,s,ByPath} + a scoped kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/otchealth/* per the Terraform capture's iam.tf -- the exact grant ssmSecret() needs, and awsCreds() prefers the ECS task-role metadata endpoint before any static key. Net effect: kvSecret() tries identity (fails fast, no IDENTITY_ENDPOINT on ECS) -> SP (fails fast, no AZURE_SP_* env) -> az-CLI (fails fast, no az binary) -> falls through to the SSM mirror and succeeds, with ZERO further code or task-def changes required. No new SSM parameters were provisioned for the 10 jobs built this session; none were needed, since they call kvSecret() with the fleet's existing global secret names, already mirrored (444 secrets, verified byte-identical in the aws-secret.mjs header). Only 3 of the original 22 (docintel-ocr-sweep, xero-health, xero-run) additionally carry working AZURE_SP_* credentials directly, because their Azure job already used SP creds rather than a managed identity -- for them the SSM fallback is a second, redundant working path, not the only one.

Elevated above plain WRITES-DUPLICATE to HIGH-RISK-CORRUPTION: this is the one job in the new-10 set that should be run supervised, one execution at a time, cloud-exclusive, never both.
